key_factors: 4-0 demolition of New Zealand on June 2 — genuine attacking quality confirmed
Haiti's first World Cup since 1974 — occasion and nerves are real factors
Scotland are in devastating form: 4-1 vs Curaçao then 4-0 vs Bolivia in final warm-up
Wilson Isidor and Jean-Ricner Bellegarde bring Premier League quality to Haiti's XI
Leverton Pierre withdrawal (replaced by Metusala) adds minor disruption to squad cohesion
reasoning: Haiti were not expected here and their 4-0 win over New Zealand showed they can perform on the big stage. Bellegarde in midfield and Isidor up front represent genuine quality. But Scotland have been absolutely devastating in warm-ups — 8 goals, multiple scorers, McTominay fully fit, a settled tactical identity. The gap in competitive experience — Haiti's first WC in 52 years versus Scotland's hunger after 28 years away — could weigh heavily on the Haitian players early. Haiti will make it competitive but a Scotland win is the most probable outcome.

Scotland's superior squad depth, outstanding pre-tournament form (8 goals in 2 warm-up wins), and experienced back four make them clear favourites. Haiti will score — Isidor and Bellegarde carry genuine Premier League quality — but cannot sustain a 90-minute battle against Scotland's press and set-piece threat. The loss of Gilmour narrows the margin but does not change the outcome. Final: Haiti 1–2 Scotland.
